organization.name: mab.xyz
organization.summary: Web3 security firm in Stockholm, described on its own website as a spin-off from Prof. Martin Monperrus' research group at KTH Royal Institute of Technology. The site lists work funded by the Ethereum Foundation, Vinnova and WASP, and a mab-xyz GitHub organization created 2025-02-14.

previousFunding.label: Ethereum Foundation 2024 Academic Grants (Sound Foundations for Client Diversity, Javier Ron and Martin Monperrus, KTH)
TheDAO Security Fund Round 1 record: mab.xyz - transaction guards

delivery.grant: TheDAO Security Fund Round 1: mab.xyz - transaction guards (organization-level match by same website and organization name)
delivery.promised: Per the mab.xyz website: open-source guards that protect users from malicious transactions. The Round 1 record states no specific deliverables. GitHub API: the public repository transaction-guard-contracts (Transaction Guard Contracts for Ethereum) was created 2026-04-08 and last pushed 2026-11-10. Whether it completes the Round 1 scope cannot be judged from the record, so no promise can be compared with a result. The repository is an existing public artifact, not matched against a stated Round 1 deliverable.

claims.claim: Geth Rebuild, a tool that checks whether official Geth releases match their source code, exists.
claims.method: GitHub API: public repository created 2024-05-06, last push 2024-11-12, 3 stars, contributors monperrus and vivi365. The DiVA page was behind a bot check and was not read. The tool was not run.

claims.claim: Vivi Andersson reported to the Geth team that build-machine file paths were left in the release and that a different compiler version was used, and the Geth team fixed its builds in 2024 and tagged her.
claims.method: GitHub API: vivi365 commented on issue 28987 on 2024-04-30 listing /home/travis paths in the release binary and on 2024-05-13 on the Ubuntu focal versus noble compiler. Pull request 30321 (build: attempt at reproducible builds) was merged 2024-08-20 by holiman and its text says cc @vivi365.

claims.claim: Reth and Lighthouse have started reproducible builds work on their own.
claims.method: GitHub API: Reth PR 10459 (reproducible build profile) merged 2024-10-22; Lighthouse PR 6799 (reproducible builds) merged 2025-05-19. Whether official releases are checkable by outsiders was not checked.

claims.claim: No client's official releases are checked by anyone outside its own team, and none of the other 11 clients has reached an externally checkable official release.
claims.method: A survey finding stated by the applicant. It would require rebuilding each client release and was not checked.

claims.claim: A single tampered build tool can silently spread to nearly all software of a Linux distribution (Julien Malka and co-authors).
claims.method: The arXiv abstract page confirms the paper title and authors (Julien Malka, Aman Sharma, Martin Monperrus and others). The finding itself was not independently reproduced.

claims.claim: The Ethereum Foundation funded the team's earlier research on client diversity.
claims.method: The EF blog lists the project Sound Foundations for Client Diversity by Javier Ron and Prof. Martin Monperrus, KTH Royal Institute of Technology.

claims.claim: CHAINS, a KTH research project financed by the Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research, funds the four KTH students' PhD research.
